Reset deletes the operator row, so after restart there is no difference to mark. A persisted implementer removed by that reset is consequently appended and pinned again. Reproduction command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-8ldq44/claude-501/limitless-routing-review-vms_t1ft/sticky.test.ts`. Output for `reset still removes saved implementer after restart`: `Expected: "codex/luna"; Received: "codex/sol"`. The assertion before reopening the Store passes.
findings.failure_scenario: The code cell contains codex/luna. An operator override selects codex/sol for an ongoing run, then is reset. Restart the daemon before the run's next model call. The resumed run stays on codex/sol instead of using the restored cell.

gold.summary: Legacy adoption trusts Git administration paths selected by an agent-controlled checkout.
Draft delivery and interrupted preparation can reuse a legacy worktree before path registration.

findings.title: Recover legacy worktrees before their path is persisted
findings.detail: The migration only checks ctx.state.worktreePath. If the previous daemon stopped during preparation after creating the worktree but before saving that path, the resumed state has no worktreePath. This guard skips registration, then prepare() calls createWorktree(), whose existing-directory branch immediately calls worktreeGit and fails with "Missing trusted Git paths". The upgrade recovery therefore misses a valid interrupted-run state.
findings.failure_scenario: The old release creates a linked worktree, then stops before preparation persists worktreePath. After upgrading, the run resumes in phase prepare with the directory present and its .git-paths record absent.

findings.title: Record legacy worktrees before the needs-human guard
findings.detail: The migration runs after the needsHumanReason guard at line 173. When that field is persisted, execution jumps into the catch block, which retries draft delivery through deliverVerifiedDraft or deliver(ctx, false). Neither path records the legacy worktree, so its Git operations still fail with "Missing trusted Git paths". This leaves the interrupted needs-human delivery case described in the request unresolved.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release persists needsHumanReason and is interrupted before draft delivery completes. After upgrading, the linked worktree has no .git-paths record. Restart skips migration, draft delivery fails, and no legacy-recording log is emitted.

findings.detail: The migration excludes every run prepared after the hard-coded sidecar commit timestamp, even when that installation was still running the previous release. Such worktrees legitimately have no sidecar, but hasLegacyWorktree returns false, so resume still fails with Missing trusted Git paths. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-legacy-migration.ts". Applying this migration to a successful prepare at 1791100000000 produced {"worktree_provenance":null} and the assertion failure: "Old-release worktree created after the sidecar commit timestamp is not eligible for adoption".
findings.failure_scenario: An installation remains on the pre-#323 release after 2026-10-04 07:35:04 UTC, creates and parks a run, then upgrades. The run's valid worktree is excluded from adoption and fails on resume.

They are absent from that cache's worktree list, or the cache does not exist. Even passing the correct source .git directory fails because legacy.ts:47 requires a bare repository. gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: Resolve rerun claims when GitHub definitively rejects the request
findings.detail: The rerun claim is persisted before the POST, but a rejected POST only throws. Subsequent inspections wait for run_attempt to advance and suppress needs-fix because the claim remains pending. A rejected request never creates that later attempt, so classification stays pending indefinitely. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-o0sYkW/claude-501/ci-review.ts`. Output: `first inspection: Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed`, followed by three `later inspection complete: false` lines and `{"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns HTTP 422 to the rerun POST. The originating workflow remains on attempt 1 forever, and every later inspection leaves the ledger in rerun_requested without emitting ci.needs_fix.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
findings.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's entire observation loop. Later PRs are skipped even though their GraphQL snapshots were fetched successfully. The same ordering repeats on subsequent polls, so a persistent CI-detail error can indefinitely suppress merge, close, review, and CI observations for other PRs. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-o0sYkW/claude-501/ci-review-poller.ts`. Output: `{"firstPrSaves":2,"secondPrSaves":0,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/main (500)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/main (500)"]}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Two PRs are tracked in one repository. The first has failed CI and its CI REST inspection returns HTTP 500; the second has a valid passing or merged snapshot. Every poll aborts on the first PR before saving the second.

findings.title: Definitively rejected reruns remain pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before POST, but every non-201 response leaves it in rerun_requested. If GitHub rejects the request, no later attempt exists to resolve that claim. Subsequent inspections suppress ci.needs_fix and keep polling indefinitely. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with a fake 422 response produced `reject Error: CI job rerun was not confirmed`, followed by `reject {"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"feed":[],"reruns":1,"mainStatusesRequested":false}` after three inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient job qualifies for rerun, but GitHub returns 422 without starting another attempt. All later observations retain the original run_attempt, leaving the failure permanently pending without actionable classification.

findings.title: Inspect main's commit statuses independently of the PR's context types
findings.detail: The shared checks helper fetches legacy commit statuses only when the PR snapshot contains status contexts or is truncated. Main can publish a failing legacy status with the same name as the PR's Actions check, so this condition hides main's failure and incorrectly permits a rerun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` against that fixture produced `main-status {"outcomes":["rerunning"],"feed":[],"reruns":1,"mainStatusesRequested":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Main has a failing legacy commit status named test, while the factory PR has a timed-out Actions check named test and no legacy status contexts. The classifier reruns the PR job and emits no ci.main_red item.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: ANSI colors bypass security-failure and timeout detection
findings.detail: Log normalization removes timestamps but preserves ANSI escapes. The anchored security and timeout patterns consequently miss colored diagnostics. A generic timed-out job containing a colored '(fail) security tests' line is rerun and recorded in the ledger, violating the security-test exclusion. Colored timeout diagnostics also fail transient classification. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a colored security failure is excluded from reruns and ledger` with `1 !== 0`, and the colored-timeout assertion produced `0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: An Actions job named 'test' times out and its logs contain '\u001b[31m(fail)\u001b[0m security tests'; its steps and annotations provide no other security-specific evidence.

findings.title: Later partial attempts strand tracked rerun results
findings.detail: Reconciliation searches only the latest workflow attempt. GitHub partial reruns can omit jobs completed in earlier attempts, so a later rerun of another job makes the tracked job disappear from this query permanently. Every subsequent inspection throws instead of recording its result. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a tracked rerun is reconciled after a later partial attempt: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job`.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A from attempt 1; A passes in attempt 2. Before polling, another failed job B is rerun in attempt 3, whose jobs response contains only B.

findings.title: Rate-limited rerun requests remain claimed forever
findings.detail: A rate-limit refusal leaves the row as 'rerun_requested'. After cooldown, reconciliation sees no newer workflow attempt, and the pending-prior branch prevents both another POST and ci.needs_fix. This permanently stalls classification even though GitHub never started a rerun. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a rate-limited POST must eventually rerun or report needs-fix: AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: posts=1, outcome=rerun_requested, needs_fix=0` after three further inspections.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns HTTP 429 for the rerun POST, then recovers. The original failed workflow remains at attempt 1.

findings.title: Main-red failures bypass the failure ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before job inspection and recordCiFailure, so these PR failures never receive the required signature, runner image, SHA, and outcome record. Pausing reactions should not discard failure evidence. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a main-red failure is still recorded in the failure ledger` with `0 !== 1`.
findings.failure_scenario: Both the default branch and a factory PR fail the non-security check 'test'; the classifier emits ci.main_red but creates no ledger row for the PR failure.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
findings.detail: A classifier exception escapes record(), aborting observation of every later PR in the repository. A persistent missing log therefore starves unrelated PRs indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: starvation {"secondSnapshot":null,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)"]}; assertion expected secondSnapshot not to be null.
findings.failure_scenario: Two tracked PRs share a repository. The first has a failed job whose logs return 404. The second never receives a saved observation, including subsequent merge, close, review, or CI changes.

findings.title: Resolve claims when rate limiting rejects the rerun
findings.detail: A rejected HTTP 429 leaves rerun_requested permanently claimed. Because no rerun actually started, run_attempt never advances; reconciliation neither retries nor emits ci.needs_fix. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output after cooldown and eight further polls: rate-limited claim {"outcome":"rerun_requested","reruns":1,"needsFix":0}; assertion expected outcome not to remain rerun_requested.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns 429 to the rerun POST, then becomes available again. The workflow remains on its original failed attempt forever, with no rerun or needs-fix result.

findings.title: Search intervening attempts when reconciling a rerun
findings.detail: Reconciliation examines only the latest workflow attempt. Attempt-specific job listings omit jobs that were not rerun in that attempt, so a subsequent partial rerun can permanently hide the factory's completed attempt. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: partial-rerun {"outcome":"rerunning","logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job"]}; expected failed_then_passed.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2 and it passes. Before the next poll, someone reruns unrelated job B in attempt 3. The classifier never reads A's passing attempt and keeps its ledger row pending.

findings.title: Observe rerun completion beyond the first 100 contexts
findings.detail: An outstanding rerun triggers inspection only when ciChanged is true. The query observes just the first 100 contexts, while REST can discover and rerun checks outside that page. Completion of such a check can leave ciKey unchanged indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: hidden rerun {"outcome":"rerunning","additionalRestCalls":0}; expected failed_then_passed.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR has 101 checks. A visible check keeps the rollup red, and the hidden check is rerun successfully. Neither the first 100 contexts nor the rollup changes, so the passing rerun is never recorded.

findings.title: Recognize standard security-test failure diagnostics
findings.detail: The security exclusion misses standard Go failure lines such as '--- FAIL: TestSecurity (0.00s)'. A generic timed-out job containing that failure is rerun and entered in the ledger, violating the security-test exclusion. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: security reruns {"reruns":1,"ledger":[..."outcome":"rerunning"...]}; assertion expected zero reruns.
findings.failure_scenario: A job named test times out after reporting a failed TestSecurity test. Its steps have generic names and there are no annotations. The classifier automatically reruns the security failure.

findings.title: Record failures suppressed by red main in the ledger
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence or recording the failure. These failures never receive the requested signature, runner image, SHA, or outcome in the ledger. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: main-red ledger []; assertion expected length 1, received length 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR fails the same check as main. The repository notification is emitted, but its failure is absent from the ledger; pushing a new SHA before main recovers loses the observation permanently.

gold.summary: Effort removal is persisted without checking policy cells hidden by operator overrides.

findings.title: Validate runtime mutations against the underlying eval policy
findings.detail: PATCH validates only the effective policy, so an operator override can hide an eval-policy reference that the patch invalidates. Resetting that override then produces no eligible candidate. On restart, Factory reads and validates the eval policy before applying operator overrides, so startup fails. DELETE similarly checks only operator cells and accepts deletion of an eval-policy model. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pqEs0s/claude-501/catalog-review.XXXXXX.ts`. Output: `PATCH accepted\nrestart policy INVALID: Unsupported effort high\n{"candidates":[],"skipped":[{"modelId":"codex/experiment@high","reason":"Error: Unsupported effort \"high\" for codex/experiment; supported: none"}]
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment supporting high and none; load an eval policy naming codex/experiment@high; override that cell with codex/sol; PATCH the experiment to support only none. The patch succeeds, resetting the override breaks routing, and restarting rejects the eval policy. Deleting the experiment al

findings.title: Deleting a file-policy model prevents daemon restart
findings.detail: Deletion checks only persisted operator cells. A runtime model referenced by routing/policy.json can therefore be deleted successfully, but Factory subsequently calls readPolicy against the reduced catalog and throws during startup. Direct reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-catalog.ts". Output: "DELETE succeeded\nrestart failed: routing/policy.json references deleted codex/experiment". The fixture installs a valid file-backed policy, deletes its runtime model, then repeats startup policy validation.
findings.failure_scenario: Add codex/experiment, reference it in routing/policy.json, load that policy, delete the model without any operator cell referencing it, then restart the daemon.

findings.title: Older probes can overwrite newer discovery results
findings.detail: Probe results are committed without a per-provider generation check or serialization. Probes can overlap because setEnabled starts a probe even when another is pending. An older response arriving last replaces the newer served set and persists it with a fresh observation timestamp. Direct reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-discovery.ts". Output: "served: [\"old-build\"]\nnew-build rejected: true". The fixture resolves the second fake probe with new-build before resolving the first with old-build.
findings.failure_scenario: A scheduled probe observes old-build but responds slowly. An enable request starts another probe after the backend changes; it returns new-build first. The older response then overwrites discovery, causing current models to be skipped until another successful probe.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Clearing the default effort silently preserves its previous value
findings.detail: An empty effort input omits effort from the PATCH payload. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges that payload over the existing model, retaining its previous effort. Saving therefore reports success without applying the edit. A diagnostic executing the extracted payload expression and backend merge returned {"payloadHasEffort":false,"resultingEffortAfterPatchMerge":"high"}.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model whose default effort is high, clear Default effort, and save. The model still defaults to high. Removing high from supported efforts at the same time instead causes validation to reject the update.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears when Setup is reopened
findings.detail: The requested recent catalog history is replaced with a page-local session signal. Only mutations made through this mounted page call record(); catalog SSE messages merely refresh snapshots. Reloading or navigating away discards all entries, and changes from another browser or the CLI never appear.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or delete a runtime model, navigate away and return to Setup. Catalog history is empty despite the recent change. A change made in another client is also absent.

findings.title: A failed routing load leaves the retry picker permanently loading
findings.detail: The rejection handler sets the error but never clears loading or provides a way to retry the fetch. The picker stays hidden and submission stays disabled even after connectivity recovers. Executing the extracted mount callback with a rejected getRouting returned {"loading":true,"error":"Error: temporary outage","retryDisabled":true}. Recovery requires closing and reopening the panel.
findings.failure_scenario: Open Retry with different models for a run without model overrides while GET /api/routing temporarily fails. Restoring connectivity does not make the open picker usable.

findings.title: Clearing default effort preserves the old value
findings.detail: An empty default-effort field omits effort from the PATCH payload. RuntimeCatalog.patch merges the payload over the existing model, so the old effort survives. Isolated execution of the submit handler confirmed patchHasEffort=false and mergedEffort="high" after clearing the field. Removing that effort from supportedEfforts simultaneously also makes the API reject the otherwise valid edit.
findings.failure_scenario: Edit a runtime model with effort="high", clear Default effort, and save. The model still defaults to high. If Supported efforts is also cleared, saving fails with model.effort: absent from efforts.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears whenever Setup unmounts
findings.detail: Catalog history comes exclusively from the component-local session signal, populated by this component's mutation callbacks. Navigating away or reloading discards every entry, and catalog changes made through another client never appear. This does not provide the requested recent catalog-change history despite live catalog refreshes.
findings.failure_scenario: Add, edit or delete a runtime model, navigate to Models, then return to Setup. Catalog history is empty even though the change remains persisted.

gold.summary: Embedded short registered secrets remain visible in digest fields.
MCP status returns private land reasons unchanged on direct and proxy backends.

findings.title: Unread PR events can hide a newly required review
findings.detail: Only three event kinds seed review candidates. After the consumer acknowledges the original PR and approval events, a new head with a stale approval is ignored when its unread event is pr.ci_passed, pr.ci_failed, or another GitHub event. Current-state reconciliation never runs for that PR. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts" new-head. Output: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0" despite the changed head requiring review.
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges an approved PR, another commit changes its head, and CI passes. The next session digest reports zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Exclude active review rounds from PRs awaiting review
findings.detail: The review eligibility predicate ignores review.rounds. A PR whose changes verdict has started a running round remains listed as awaiting review because its approval is absent or stale. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts" active-round. Output: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0" while round1 is running.
findings.failure_scenario: The original PR-opened event remains unread while a requested review round is queued or running. Every session digest incorrectly asks for another review before the revised work is delivered.

findings.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the landed predicate never checks it. resolveMergedRun preserves succeeded status and can record a confirmed merge without creating a PR snapshot or a merged resolution. Status then reports an unknown or reviewable PR despite confirmed delivery. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts" merged-status. Output: "Confirmed merged run: PR state unknown; Inspect the PR and await a saved observation before reviewing or landing."
findings.failure_scenario: Merge reconciliation confirms an externally merged succeeded run whose saved PR snapshot is absent or stale, with no landed queue entry. limitless_status fails to report it as landed.

findings.title: Honor the run's persisted merge flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the merged-state check never considers it. Existing auto-merge delivery and GitHub reconciliation persist merged=true without necessarily saving a PR snapshot or land entry. The new tool consequently reports an already merged PR as unknown or needing review. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.test.ts"`. Probe output: Expected: "Landed"; Received: "PR state unknown".
findings.failure_scenario: A succeeded run has merged=true after automatic delivery, prSnapshot=null, no merged resolution, and no land entry. limitless_status instructs the agent to await an observation instead of reporting completion.

findings.title: Consider new PR events when discovering pending reviews
findings.detail: Only PR-opened, round-delivered and approval events seed the review candidates. After those events are acknowledged, subsequent CI or comment events never cause the current review state to be inspected. A changed head with a stale approval is therefore silently omitted. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.test.ts"`. Probe output: Expected: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0"; Received: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.failure_scenario: The consumer acknowledges a PR's opening and approval. Someone pushes another commit, invalidating the approval, and polling emits pr.ci_passed for that head. The next session digest reports zero PRs awaiting review.

findings.title: Exclude active changes rounds from reviews awaiting action
findings.detail: The review eligibility check ignores review.rounds. An unread PR-opened event remains listed as awaiting review while a requested changes round is queued or running, although limitless_status correctly reports that work is in progress. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.test.ts"`. Probe output: Expected: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0"; Received: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0". A separate real-Store probe reproduced this with a queued review round.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR is opened, the reviewer requests changes without acknowledging its opening event, and the factory queues a review round. SessionStart continues presenting the original head as awaiting review.

gold.summary: Layered URL and Unicode encodings bypass the single-pass private-text decoder.

findings.title: Honor the run's persisted merged flag

findings.title: Recursive status still executes submodule configuration
findings.detail: The isolated git directory protects only the top-level repository. Status recursively inspects initialized submodules using their own repository configuration, while safe_git blanks only filter keys discovered in the isolated repository. A submodule clean filter therefore executes after checks. A filter that normalizes changed bytes back to the indexed contents also makes this status return empty. Probe command: python3 "$TMPDIR/review-submodule-status.py". Output: "status output: ''" followed by "AssertionError: isolated status executed the submodule clean filter". This exposure also existed in the previous status path.
findings.failure_scenario: The landing commit contains an initialized submodule. Checks plant filter.attack.clean in that submodule's config and modify a same-length tracked file selected by its .gitattributes. The post-check isolated status executes the planted command and can report a clean tree.

findings.title: Handle retired IDs in persisted routing overrides before removing the model
findings.detail: Factory constructs RuntimePolicy at startup, which validates every saved routing cell against the current catalog. findings.title: Preserve eval resume compatibility instead of asserting rejection
findings.detail: The new compatibility test explicitly expects HTTP 400 when resuming an interrupted eval containing an unknown historical model. EvalRunner.resume revalidates the entire stored request through submit, so one removed target prevents all remaining work from continuing, including work for supported targets. This contradicts the requirement that records written before the change still resume.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted eval created before the upgrade contains both the removed model and a supported model. After upgrading, eval resume rejects the complete request with 'unknown model ID', so unfinished trials for the supported model cannot continue.

findings.title: Interrupted legacy evals cannot resume
findings.detail: The new compatibility test explicitly expects HTTP 400 when resuming an eval containing an unknown model. EvalRunner.resume resubmits the entire stored request, and validateRequest rejects the removed ID before completed trials can be reused or remaining valid targets scheduled. This contradicts the requirement that existing records still resume. A mixed eval is entirely blocked even when the removed model's trials have already finished.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted eval contains completed trials for the machine-named provider and pending trials for a retained provider. After upgrading, its resume endpoint returns 400 with an unknown-model error.

findings.title: Historical model pins block unrelated catalog edits
findings.detail: Every runtime model addition or patch revalidates every historical run against the current catalog. Removing this model makes previously valid run pins fail that validation, so an old run prevents unrelated catalog changes indefinitely, even if its chain includes a valid fallback. A targeted invocation of RuntimeCatalog.add with a historical retired-lan/legacy pin produced: run historical-run: Error: models.triage entry "retired-lan/legacy": Error: unknown model ID "retired-lan/legacy".
findings.failure_scenario: The database contains a completed run pinned to the removed model. Adding or patching an unrelated runtime model fails because the completed run still references that model.

findings.title: Runtime models belonging to the removed provider prevent startup
findings.detail: Factory construction throws for any persisted runtime model whose provider is absent from providerDefs. The new restart test seeds enablement and speed overrides but misses runtime model definitions.
findings.failure_scenario: Before upgrading, a runtime model was registered under the machine-named provider. On the next startup, Factory throws "unknown provider" while loading runtime_models, making all runs and provider listings unavailable.
